mission: SaferAI builds risk-measurement tools for governments and companies: quantitative risk models that turn AI capabilities into estimates of real-world harm, public ratings of how well AI companies manage risk, and contributions to standards at the OECD, NIST, ISO and the EU AI Act.

key_work.title: AI company risk-management ratings
key_work.plain_summary: The first public ratings of AI companies' risk management: even leaders scored only 'moderate' or 'weak' (Anthropic 2.2/5), while xAI scored 0.

key_work.title: Frontier Risk Management Tracker
key_work.plain_summary: An updated, side-by-side comparison of 12 companies' safety frameworks on 65+ risk-management criteria.

key_work.title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling
key_work.plain_summary: Sets out what rigorous, numbers-based risk modelling for advanced AI should look like, drawing on a 22-expert workshop.

key_work.title: GLM-5.2 Risk Evaluation Report
key_work.plain_summary: An independent European evaluation of Zhipu AI's open-weight model, finding frontier-level cyber and biology capability without the safeguards frontier developers use.

key_work.title: Lessons from External Review of DeepMind's Scheming Inability Safety Case
key_work.plain_summary: An outside review of Google DeepMind's argument that its models cannot yet scheme, and what such reviews teach.

status_note: French association (loi 1901); founder Siméon Campos started the work in 2022 and stepped back to advisor/board chair in late 2025; Henry Papadatos is Executive Director
status_raw: active — French association (loi 1901); founder Siméon Campos started the work in 2022 and stepped back to advisor/board chair in late 2025; Henry Papadatos is Executive Director

warnings.text: All rated AI companies have weak to very weak risk management practices.
Open-weight models can reach frontier cyber and biology capabilities without safeguards.
AI risk assessment is still mostly qualitative, making thresholds hard to set.

recommendations.text: Adopt risk-management practices from high-risk industries like aviation and finance.
Move to quantitative risk models that map benchmark results to probabilities of harm.
Make companies comply with their own safety frameworks and subject them to external review.
